1. Executive summary
1.1. On 2024 July 8, Richmond Environmental Services Limited (RESL) made an application to
the Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR) for an Amual Price Adjustment Mechanism
(ANPAM) adjustment of 3.06 % to be applied to its base rates and charges.
1.2. The OUR has reviewed and examined the required ANPAM adjustment and has set out its
findings in this Determination Notice.
1.3. The OUR has verified the infomation presented in RESL's submission and confirms the
proposedANPAMrateadjustmentof3.06%,whichistobeappliedtotheapprovedwaterand
sewerage rates. This adjustment is in keeping with the requirements specified in Richmond
Environmental Services Limited - Water and Sewerage Rates Determination Notice,
document number 2023/WAS/002mET.00l , which addresses the application of the Price
Adj ustment Mechanism.
1.4. The ANPAM rate adjustment is a rebasing of a specific set of indices only. The adjustment is
applicable to customers' 2024 July consumption, which will be reflected in 2024 August
billing cycle.
I .5. The new base indices for the Price Adjustment Mechanism (PAM) are as follows:
• Foreign Exchange Rate: J$156.97 to US$1.00
• Consumer price Index: 134.90
• Electricity charge: $56.5M{Wh
1.6. The new base indices will remain in effect until the next programmed reset of the ANPAM in
2025 June or the implementation of new tariffs, whichever is earlier.
1.7. The new base rates and fees are displayed in Table I.1 below and will become effective for
the 2024 August billing cycle.

2. Introduction
2.I. On 2024 July 8, RIchmond Environmental Services Limited (RESL) made an application to
the Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR) for an Annual Price Adjustment Mechanism
(ANPAM) rate adjustment of 3.06%. The ANPAM rate adjustment request is consistent with
the determinations made in the Richmond Environmental Service Limited - Water and
Sewerage Rates Determination Notice, document number 2023/WAS/002/DET.001, issued
2023 June 30 ("Determination Notice").
2.2. In the Determination Notice, RESL was granted approval to implement a monthly PAM, as a
component of customers' bills.
2.3. The Price Adjustment Mechanism (PAM) captures the effect of movements in three (3)
indices associated with RESL' s major input costs, over which it has no control.
2.4. In particular, the mechanism is predicated on the assumption that RESL has no control over
inflation, the movement of the Jamaican dollar relative to its United States Dollar counterpart,
and electricity prices. The changes in RESL's PAM are captured in the following three (3)
indices:
• Consumer price Index (CPI),
• Foreign exchange rate (FX): the Jamaican dollar (JS) exchange rate relative to the
United States Dollar (USS); and
• Electricity prices expressed as sncwh).
2.5. The PAM rate adjustment is applied to customers' bills monthly. The mechanism allows for
an adjustment of base rates by rolling in the cumulative monthly PAM rate into the base rates
and charges. This process generally occurs on an annual basis. The annual reset is referred to
as the Annual Price Adjustment Mechanism (ANPAM).
2.6. The main objective of the armual reset is to minimize the monthly PAM differential
adjustment, which accounts for the variation between the current and the base values for the
three (3) indices on customers' bills.

3. Legal Framework
3.1. RESL is regulated by the Office of Utilities Regulation Act and operates under the following
licences (collectively referred to as the Licences):
• RIchmond Environmental Services Limited Water Supply Licence, 2013
• Richmond Environmental Services Limited Sewerage Service Licence, 2013
3.2. The role and function of the OUR in the water and sewerage sector is governed by the
provisions of the OUR Act. Section 4(1) (a) of the OUR Act, provides that the OUR is
en:poweled to "regulate the provision of prescribed utility services by licensees or specified
orgr#j.zcr/j.o#s ". The provision of sewerage services and the supply and distribution of water
are included among the prescribed utility services defined in the First Schedule of the OUR
Act.
3 .3 . Section 4(4) of the OUR Act expressly authorizes the OUR to determine the rates charged for
the provision of a prescribed service. The section reads:
" (4) The oJf ice shall have power to determine, in accordance with the provisions
of this Act, the rates or fares which may be charged in respect Of the provisions of a
prescribed utility service. "
3.4. In exercise of its powers to determine rates, the OUR issued the Determination Notice, which
sets out the approved rates and charges for RESL's services. The Determination Notice also
makes allowance for an annual price adjustment.
3.5. In keeping with the determination regarding the armual reset of the PAM, RESL has now
applied for an ANPAM rate adjustment to its base rates and charges.

4. The ouR's Analysis
4. I . The OUR's review and detemiination of rates is guided by the principle that rates should be
sufficient to cover prudently incuned costs. In this regard, the monthly and annual price
adjustment mechanisms are designed to align the rates with input prudently incured cost.
The Price Adjustment Mechanism
4.2. The PAM allows RESL to adjust its rates, monthly to account for the effect of changes in
input costs that are exogenous to its operations. It, therefore, seeks to preserve RESL rates in
real terms against monthly fluctuations in its input costs, due to changes in inflation, foreign
exchange rate movements and changes in electricity rates.
4.3. The mathematical computation of the PAM is as follows:
PAM = (Wfx*AFX+wcpi*ACPI+wkwh*Akwh)* 100
VAere:
AFX is the monthly percentage change in the JS/USS exchange rate,
ACPI is the monthly percentage change in the CPI,
Akwh is the monthly percentage in the kilowatt hour charge for electricity,
wfx is the approved weight for the JS/USS exchange rate,
wcpi is the approved weight for the CPI, and
wkwh is the approved weight for the kilowatt hour charge for electricity.
4.4. The ANPAM normally allows for an adjustment of base rates and charges each year. This is
achieved by the `rolling-in' of the cumulative PAM rate from the time of last ANPAM
adjustment into the base rates. The calculated ANPAM rate reflects the weighted change in
the base values for the three (3) components in the mechanism, since the last ANPAM
adjustment.
4.5. Mathematically, the new base rates may be expressed as follows:
New Base Rate = Current Base Rate *(1 + ANPAM adjustment rate).
4.6. RESL's ANPAM adjustment rate, which is to be reflected on customers' bills as of 2024
August is 3.06%. Table 4.I below shows the details of the computation, which have been
verified by the OUR.
4.7. The source of the input data is as follows:
• Statistical Institute of Jamaica (STATIN) for Consumer Price Index (CPI);
• Bank of Jamaica (BOJ) for foreign exchange (FX) rate (JS:USS); and
• RESL's electricity bills for the month of 2024 May, to ascertain the electricity
component.
